subject: Verify routing's startup by the session file's tail, and never trust a reload
diff_check: clean change.diff is the commit diff (git diff parent commit -- paths); the seeded change.diff replaces both added lines of trustStartedSession (src read-only-session.ts and dist read-only-session.js) and applies with patch -p1 to an archive of the parent, reproducing the seeded tree (checked)
class_note: Requested class was security (startup verification skipped or misread). Not shown: routing state is built from Pi's in-memory branch, not from file bytes, so a wrong check lets an in-memory-only entry count as persisted after a failed write. That is an integrity error with no hostile actor and no trust boundary crossed. Built as logic at the lead's instruction.

clean.description: The change as committed. No defect is planted.

seeded.description: The reload guard in trustStartedSession is inverted to a truthiness test: `reason !== "reload"` becomes `reason`. A reload (reason "reload", which is truthy) now sets a trust point although Pi did not re-read the file. After a failed write, memory can hold an entry the file lacks and routing would treat it as persisted. The commit's rule is that a reload establishes no trust point. The dist file is mirrored so the committed tests, which import dist, exercise the seed.
seeded.rule_quoted: requirements.md item 4: "A session start that Pi reports as a reload establishes no trust point, because the session stays in memory and the file is not re-read. A trust point from before the reload still applies after it."

proof.method: logic: the committed startup-verification test passes on clean and fails on seeded
